title: The event loop
idea: Node runs your JavaScript on one thread. The event loop hands it finished background work, one callback at a time, whenever the stack is empty.

analogy.text: A restaurant with one waiter and a busy kitchen. The waiter never cooks: he takes orders and delivers each dish the moment it is ready.
analogy.breaks: If the waiter stalls on one table, every other table waits.

points: Your JavaScript runs on a single thread, one task at a time.
Slow work (timers, files, network) is handed to libuv and the OS.
Finished work queues a callback; the loop runs it when the stack is empty.
Promise callbacks (microtasks) jump the queue before the next timer.

steps.caption: The script starts. main() sits on the call stack.
Line 1 runs at once and prints A.
Line 2: setTimeout hands the timer to libuv and moves on. It does not wait.
Line 3: the promise is already resolved, so its callback is queued as a microtask.
Line 4 runs at once and prints D. All of this was synchronous.
The script ends. The stack is empty, so the loop looks for work. Microtasks go first.
The loop runs the microtask: C prints.
The 0 ms timer has finished, so libuv queues its callback.
Stack empty, no microtasks left: the loop takes the timer callback. B prints last.
Order: A D C B. Synchronous code, then microtasks, then timers.

code.title: Order of output
code.caption: Run it. Then move the last console.log above the Promise line and predict again.

code.title: nextTick vs promise
code.caption: process.nextTick has its own queue, drained before promise callbacks (CommonJS).

pitfalls: A long loop blocks the thread: timers, requests and everything else wait.
`setTimeout(fn, 0)` is not instant. It still waits for the stack to clear.
CPU-heavy work belongs in a worker thread or another process.

quiz.q: In the first snippet, what order does it print?
quiz.why: Synchronous code first (A, D), then the microtask (C), then the timer callback (B).

takeaway: One thread, many waiting jobs: sync first, microtasks next, timers after.

starters: Why do promises run before setTimeout?
How do I avoid blocking the event loop?
